answer_text:
Let  

\[
V_d=H^0(\mathbb{P}^n,\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^n}(d))
\]

be the vector space of homogeneous polynomials of degree \(d\) in \(n+1\) variables. Its dimension is

\[
\dim V_d=\binom{d+n}{d}.
\]

A degree \(d\) hypersurface in \(\mathbb{P}^n\) is a nonzero element of \(V_d\) up to scalar, so the family of all degree \(d\) hypersurfaces is parametrized by the projective space

\[
\mathbb{P}(V_d)\cong \mathbb{P}^{\binom{d+n}{d}-1}.
\]

Now impose the condition that the hypersurface contain a point \(p_i\in \mathbb{P}^n\). If \(F\in V_d\) is a degree \(d\) homogeneous polynomial, the condition

\[
F(p_i)=0
\]

is a single linear condition on \(F\). Thus each generic point cuts out a hyperplane in \(\mathbb{P}(V_d)\).

We are given

\[
m=\binom{d+n}{d}-1=\dim \mathbb{P}(V_d)
\]

generic points. For generic points, the corresponding \(m\) linear conditions are independent. Therefore they cut \(\mathbb{P}(V_d)\) down to

\[
\dim \mathbb{P}(V_d)-m=0,
\]

i.e. to a single point of \(\mathbb{P}(V_d)\).

Hence there is exactly one degree \(d\) hypersurface containing a generic set of \(\binom{d+n}{d}-1\) points.

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
